To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the knowledge needs of software development teams are highly task-oriented and (2) the right approach for distributed software development teams using an agile process is to provide a system that supports the capture of information needs and their pro-active distribution, and that allows for an incremental organizational learning approach for knowledge capture.

(1) the knowledge management needs of agile software processes can be addressed with a system that supports the capture and pro-active delivery of recurrent information needs, and (2) this system should facilitate an incremental organizational learning approach to capture and maintain what documentation/information developers actually need, such that documentation and information can be created “as needed” instead of on an ad hoc basis.

the following three factors are important for the success of agile processes in a distributed setting: (i) the use of a shared workspace for the development of a software product, (ii) the use of an information distribution tool that supports the capture and pro-active dissemination of recurrent information needs, and (iii) the use of lightweight documentation that is tailored to the needs of the developers.

developing an organizational memory that supports agile software processes.
the question of how the benefits of agile software development can be leveraged in distributed software development teams.
developing a system that supports the knowledge management needs of distributed agile software processes.
